result.title: Prospective Hindsight: Self-Calibrating Reinforcement Learning via Prediction-Reality Gaps
result.summary: Reinforcement learning for long-horizon agents relies on purely retrospective training signals: credit is assigned only after observing environmental consequences, leaving the agent's belief at action time invisible to the gradient. We introduce Prospective Hindsight (PH), a self-calibrating training principle that augments any retrospective base method with a signal derived from the gap between the agent's prospective prediction (before feedback) and the retrospective evaluation (after feedback). This per-rollout surprise identifies samples where the agent's self-model is most inaccurate and amplifies their gradient contribution through a stop-gradient surprise-weighted advantage. Since the prospective predictor shares parameters with the policy, the two co-evolve, progressively shifting focus to the agent's remaining blind spots. We connect this principle to a privileged-information gap and show that minimizing the surprise residual provides a descent pathway on the agent's miscalibration rate; calibration thus emerges as a byproduct of optimization rather than from an added objective. On single-turn verifiable tasks and a multi-turn personal-agent task (under GRPO, on-policy distillation, and their combination), PH improves both task performance and calibration, with consistent gains across model scales. Notably, the dominant miscalibration mode shifts structurally between regimes, overconfident failures in single-turn, underconfident successes in multi-turn, yet the same training principle addresses both successfully.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 Prospective Hindsight（PH）自校准训练原则：在任意回顾式 RL 方法上，用「反馈前的前瞻预测」与「反馈后的回顾评估」之间的差距构造逐轨迹 surprise，并以 stop-gradient 加权优势放大自模型最不准样本的梯度，使策略与预测器共同演化、校准作为优化副产品出现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心概念——动作时刻的信念状态、预测与现实差距驱动的监督权重——可能启发 LVR 中的贡献分配与证据筛选：可核查 latent 推理是否也应按「预测误差/惊讶度」加权训练，以及自校准是否能对应 latent 状态的动态停止或证据获取决策。
